summary: Draft Session Manager Kernel record. `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `0`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and was later carried forward by source-enrichment as a docs-first current-build kernel candidate with a `power-request-simulation` trigger recommendation. Adjacent Microsoft docs later documented the public timer-resolution contract, including system-wide `ExSetTimerResolution` behavior and the Windows 10 2004+ change that `timeBeginPeriod` no longer globally affects unrelated processes, but no current Microsoft page has been found that names this exact internal registry seed. A later KVM local-KD pass then showed the live current-build global `KiGlobalTimerResolutionRequests = 0`, aligning the running kernel with the repo-doc default, and a later current-build INIT descriptor scan found the matching `Session Manager\\Kernel` binding row for the same global RVA. The broad lightweight runtime batch then wrote the candidate value as `1` and still returned `zero-exact-target-hits`, while a later repo-native follow-up added an explicit `power-request-simulation` harness to both the generic Procmon guest tool and the mega-trigger runtime surface. The 2026-04-18 runtime sprint then ran the intended lane order on the KVM guest: ETW produced only helper-query resolver hits, Procmon failed at `SaveAs`, and a clean QGA-launched WPR boot-registry rerun completed end-to-end and retained 101 `Session Manager\\Kernel` subtree hit lines with zero exact `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` value hits and an empty normalized bundle. The lane is strong enough for a schema-backed draft, but still lacks an exact runtime registry read and Microsoft documentation for the exact internal registry seed. A 2026-04-23 KVM Ghidra static batch retained the `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` ntoskrnl string seed but left the function/xref path static-context-only, so the runtime/read gap remains open. A 2026-04-23 quoted KVM ETW stackwalk rerun fixed the guest helper `reg.exe` quoting path and captured an exact `RegQueryValue` event for `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests`, with status `0xC0000034` because the value is absent; this validates the parser and target filter but remains helper-triggered rather than kernel boot-consumer proof.

The open part is still the exact runtime registry-read proof and the external Microsoft documentation gap for this internal seed.

setting.name: Global Timer Resolution Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-level Session Manager setting tied to how the kernel handles global timer-resolution requests. It is kernel-adjacent and is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel researchers may inspect this value when investigating timer-resolution behavior, power-request interactions, or undocumented timer-policy tuning.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value now has a stronger docs-first evidence chain because it has repo docs, baseline state, exact current-build string presence, adjacent Microsoft documentation for the public timer-resolution contract, a live current-build KD value that matches the repo-doc default, a current-build INIT descriptor binding for the same global, a repo-native `power-request-simulation` harness, a weak ETW follow-up, an environment-sensitive Procmon export failure, and a clean QGA/WPR boot-registry rerun that retained Session Manager Kernel subtree activity with zero exact value hits. It is still too weak for a published tweak because exact runtime registry-read proof and first-party documentation for this internal registry seed remain open.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs assign `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests = 0` under `Session Manager\\Kernel` and map it to `KiGlobalTimerResolutionRequests`. The observed clean baseline later confirmed that the parent key exists while the value itself is absent. The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` in `ntoskrnl.exe`. Later source-enrichment kept the candidate in the canonical queue with the same docs-first route bucket and, unlike many raw docs-only leads, converged on a concrete low-priority trigger family: `power-request-simulation`, with suggested primitives such as `PowerCreateRequest(SystemRequired)`, `PowerSetRequest(DisplayRequired)`, and an audio playback session. Microsoft later documented the public timer-resolution family from two useful angles: `ExSetTimerResolution` still describes system-wide clock-interrupt frequency changes and their battery/performance impact, while the multimedia timer guidance notes that starting with Windows 10, version 2004, `timeBeginPeriod` no longer affects timer resolution globally across unrelated processes. Those pages are strong current-build family context, but they do not name `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` itself or publish an internal `Session Manager\\Kernel` registry contract. A later KVM local-KD pass then resolved `nt!KiGlobalTimerResolutionRequests` in the live current-build kernel and returned `0`, which matches the repo-doc default and removes the older live-state gap. A later host-side current-build INIT descriptor scan then found the `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` UTF-16 string in the `INIT` section and one nearby `Session Manager\\Kernel` descriptor row at file offset `0xbed488` pointing at static RVA `0xFC5C48`, matching the live KD RVA for `nt!KiGlobalTimerResolutionRequests`. The broad tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane still wrote all 21 `Session Manager\\Kernel` batch values, including `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and returned `zero-exact-target-hits` for this specific candidate in the ETW-derived query surface. A later repo-native follow-up then closed the old trigger-design gap by adding `power-request-simulation` as a named guest Procmon profile plus a matching mega-trigger runtime alias, reusing the same `PowerCreateRequest` and `PowerSetRequest` primitive family that source-enrichment had already recommended. The 2026-04-18 ETW-first pass produced real guest ETW/XML artifacts but retained only helper-side `reg.exe query` lines, so it remained resolver-only rather than target proof. The same sprint then tried the matching Procmon support lane, but `Procmon SaveAs` timed out before CSV export completed. A final QGA-launched WPR boot-registry rerun then completed cleanly, rebooted the guest, generated a full tracerpt CSV, and retained 101 `Session Manager\\Kernel` subtree lines while still retaining zero exact `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` value hits. The normalized bundle for that clean rerun exists and reports `event_count = 0`, which removes the old timeout ambiguity but still does not close the exact runtime-read gap. The next proof step is no longer a broader rerun of the same family. It is a narrower exact-read runtime lane that can show whether the Session Manager Kernel descriptor consumer still performs a value-level read on modern builds or whether the subtree activity is now generic boot-time context only.

evidence.summary: After fixing the guest ETW stackwalk helper to quote native arguments, a QGA-launched 45-second capture produced a physical ETL and normalized bundle. The bundle contains one exact `RegQueryValue` event for `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Kernel` / `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests`, with caller stack frames through `reg.exe`, `KernelBase.dll`, `ntdll.dll`, and `ntoskrnl.exe`; the returned status indicates the value is absent on the baseline. This upgrades the tooling/parser proof while leaving the kernel boot-consumer question open.

decision.why: The candidate is strong enough for a schema-backed draft because it has a repo-doc default, observed baseline state, a current-build string hit, adjacent Microsoft documentation for the timer-resolution feature family, a live current-build KD value that matches the repo-doc default, a current-build INIT descriptor binding from `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` to the same live global, a concrete enrichment-recommended trigger family that is now mirrored by a repo-native harness, an ETW-first pass, a Procmon support attempt, and now a clean QGA/WPR boot-registry rerun that retains only Session Manager Kernel subtree activity with zero exact value hits. The 2026-04-18 review keeps this blocked because repeated targeted runtime capture still provides no exact current-build registry-read pivot, and Microsoft still does not publish the exact internal `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` registry contract. Further chase should wait for a narrower exact-read trace pivot rather than another broad replay of the same negative-result family.
decision.promotion_disposition_reason: Closed as rejected for app/research-provider promotion because the remaining evidence gap is intentional: current-build exact reads, safe trigger conditions, authoritative semantics, or boot-safe validation are still missing.
decision.promotion_reopen_criteria: Reopen only with a safer current-build lane that proves exact target consumption and resolves the listed intentional-hold blockers.
